Requirements estimated from maintenance of the body pool of ascorbate
An alternative approach to estimating requirements is to determine the fractional rate of catabolism of total body ascorbate; an
appropriate intake would then be that required to replace losses and maintain the body pool.
Clinical signs of scurvy are seen when the total body pool of ascorbate is below 1.7 mmol (300 mg). The pool increases with
intake, reaching a maximum of approximately 8.5 mmol (1500 mg) in adultsd114 mmol (20 mg) per kg bodyweight. The basis
for the 1989 United States Recommended Daily Amount (US RDA) of 60 mg was the observed mean fractional turnover rate of
3.2% of a body pool of 20 mg per kg bodyweight per day, with allowances for incomplete absorption of dietary ascorbate and indi-
vidual variation.
It has been argued that a total body pool of 5.1 mmol (900 mg) is adequate; it is threefold higher than the minimum required to
prevent scurvy, and there is no evidence that there are any health beneﬁts from a body pool greater than 600 mg. The observed body
